key_insight: Mosaic extends agentic reinforcement learning to multi-session trajectories by assigning credit across sessions instead of treating an entire trajectory as one undifferentiated training unit.
engineering_relevance: This matters for agentic systems that use context compaction or subagent forking, where training should match deployment behavior and optimize how sessions are allocated and reused.
method: Critic-free hierarchical optimization for multi-session RL
Trajectory-level advantage estimation with session-usage signals
Session-level advantage shaping via estimated marginal contribution
evidence_signal: On BrowseComp with Qwen3.5-4B, Mosaic outperforms broadcast-style training in both context compaction and subagent forking, while using fewer sessions on average.
watch_item: Estimated marginal contributions and session-usage signals may be sensitive to noisy credit assignment, so the method could require careful tuning and stable session-level measurement.
